newsitem.title: UK: Calm returns to Euro-markets, stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: Calm returns to Euro-markets, stocks rise.

text.p: European markets rebounded on Monday as the turmoil of recent days subsided, at least temporarily, following an EU stability pact deal and a strong start on Wall Street.
An accord between European Union leaders in Dublin on a mechanism for ensuring monetary discipline after the launch of a single currency in 1999 boosted bond markets and the dollar in early trade.
That, in turn, helped stock markets recover ground after last week's volatility and Wall Street firmed on news of a merger between aerospace giants Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.

German stocks closed floor trade two percent higher, outpacing gains on Europe's other two biggest bourses -- London and Paris. By the time European markets closed, the Dow Industrial Average was up about 30 points.

Despite the return of a measure of calm to European markets, investors remained wary ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee, even though most analysts did not expect any immediate rise in U.S. interest rates.
The dollar closed higher in Europe, underpinned by mark weakness in the wake of the stability pact accord.

Analysts said the pact bolstered optimism that Europe's single currency project would go ahead on time in 1999 and increased the chance of a broad-based economic and monetary union (EMU) that would include Italy and Spain.
It was also seen lowering Europe's interest rate horizon, thereby buoying the dollar and yen against European currencies.
"The weekend news argues in favour of a stronger dollar into the end of the year," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.
By 1700 GMT the dollar was quoted around 1.5525 marks and 114.17 yen, compared with 1.5473 and 113.95 in late business on Friday.

Government bond markets gained initially on the news from Dublin but German Bunds lost ground on the release of U.S. data that showed November industrial production posted the largest gain in nine months. British bonds also ended flat after the market failed to hold early gains.
The London, Paris and Frankfurt equity markets all shot higher at the start but only Frankfurt managed to sustain the pace in thin trade.

Germany's 30-share DAX index zoomed 56 points in floor trade, closing two percent up at 2,855.79. The IBIS DAX was unable to gain further in later computerised trade, ending 25 points higher at 2,841.
"Investors are still holding back a bit. Some think there is still room for a correction down to 2,750," one Frankfurt trader said.
Industrial giant Daimler Benz AG, whose Dasa unit is one of the partners in the Airbus aircraft-maker, fell on news that rivals McDonnell Douglas and Boeing were to merge.
The stock pulled back later to trade at 100.95, 2.15 marks up on the day, as initial fears of the impact on Airbus were seen as overdone.
Europe's biggest share market, London, made a late rally to close at its highest levels of the day. The FTSE 100 index closed up 21.4 points, or 0.54 percent, at 3,993.8.
Volume was thin, however, and traders said investors were still cautious of another possible sell-off in New York.
"At the end of the day we still have quite a bit of uncertainty. People are reluctant to buy at what could be the top of the market," one dealer said.
French stocks also rebounded but closed well off their highs, with the CAC-40 index ending 19.16 points, or 0.87 percent, higher at 2,222.57.

Traders said market sentiment was positive but investors were feeling wary ahead of the Bank of France's annual news conference on Tuesday, the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting and a Bundesbank council meeting this week.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5525 marks and 114.17 yen compared with 1.5473 and 113.95 in late business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of top British shares closed up 21.4, or 0.54 percent, at 3,993.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index ended up 19.16 points, or 0.87 percent, at 2,222.57.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX ended floor trade up 56.08 points at 2,855.79. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX index ended 25.39 points higher at at 2,841.16.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold finished weaker at $367.55, down $2.00 from Friday's London close. Silver closed three cents off at $4.80.
